source.title: Implicit regularization of deep residual networks towards neural ODEs
source.authors: P. Marion; Yu-Han Wu; M. E. Sander; Gérard Biau

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The CIFAR-10 experiments report training accuracy after training residual convolutional networks from specified initializations, bearing on whether training error becomes small. They do not reproduce the benchmark or corrupted-label settings in V1.
record.gate_note: The synthetic-data loss-decay experiment is not a classification-error result. The paper does not compare plain networks with residual networks or test normalization as an intervention.
record.test_reason: Table 1 measures CIFAR-10 training classification accuracy after SGD in a new setting: 256 residual blocks with 1/L scaling, batch normalization, and varying activations and initializations. These results bear on V1, but do not establish that the networks satisfy its sufficient-capacity qualification.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the empirical performance gap but omits the main theoretical conclusion: appropriately scaled and initialized residual networks retain a neural ODE limit under finite-horizon gradient flow; under additional conditions, linear width overparameterization yields global convergence and an interpolating ODE limit. GELU with weight-tied initialization gives reasonable CIFAR-10 accuracy with smooth weights, while settings with non-smooth weights improve accuracy.
record.recipe_differences: The study examines neural ODE structure and weight smoothness in deep residual networks, rather than the original studies' random-label fitting or benchmark training-error comparisons. The CIFAR-10 experiment uses stochastic gradient descent, cross-entropy loss, and 180 epochs.
record.method_sensitivity: On CIFAR-10, reported training accuracy varies with activation function and initialization scheme.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorem 6 proves exponential squared-loss convergence and interpolation under specified width, depth, data, initialization, and small-target assumptions; Figure 2 illustrates synthetic regression loss approaching zero.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Appropriately initialized and scaled wide residual networks can interpolate regression data under gradient flow.

fits_no_version.finding: Smooth activations with weight-tied initialization preserve smoothness across layers and a neural ODE structure; i.i.d. initialization or ReLU can lose that structure.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initialization and activation smoothness determine whether trained scaled residual networks retain a neural ODE limit.

record.problems: The CIFAR-10 results report accuracy rather than training error directly; the reported values are medians and interquartile ranges over 5 runs. Width is not stated in the supplied text, and there is no comparison to a plain network or to CIFAR-100 and corrupted-label training.
record.rows_left_out: Test accuracy values in Table 1 were left out because the versions concern training classification error. Figure 2's synthetic-data loss decay is not a classification-error result.

untested.parts: CIFAR-100, corrupted or random classification labels, Adam, capacity sweeps establishing sufficient size, longer training to convergence, and controlled comparisons of early stopping or regularization.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student local minima and the effect of adding one or two student neurons.
Training-error comparisons across depths and between plain and residual networks; special initialization of plain tanh networks; Fixup.
Activation-matched initialization effects on signal or gradient propagation, training speed, or trainable depth in plain networks; orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization.
Learning rates relative to a measured stability threshold, loss catapults, curvature reduction, edge-of-stability dynamics, and divergence.
Training speed and learning-rate tolerance with versus without batch normalization, and comparisons with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: Training error is directly recoverable as 100% minus training accuracy. No baseline is required for this absolute fitting measure. Initialization comparisons here do not test V4's plain-network speed or trainable-depth claim, and using batch normalization does not test V6. The study is not an original source for any version.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, SGD versus Adam comparisons, model-size sweeps, early stopping, and regularized recipes.

tranche.reason: The scaled, weight-tied convolutional residual architecture is a new setting with measured CIFAR-10 training accuracy bearing on V1; the main research question concerns neural ODE structure.

source_check.notes: Errors are calculated as 100 minus Table 1 accuracy; uncertainties are interquartile ranges over five runs. Appendix E specifies 16 output channels in the first convolution; sufficient capacity and longer-training convergence are untested for these CIFAR-10 runs.
